business_problem: Diagnosing coronary artery disease from coronary CTA scans is labor-intensive, can take hours for specialists, and often yields subjective conclusions, creating a need for faster, more objective functional assessment and earlier detection of clinically significant disease.
solution_summary: Heartflow built an in-house AI diagnostic platform for coronary artery disease that starts with raw coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) image sets uploaded from CT scanners. The Heartflow platform processes thousands to tens of thousands of images per case, reconstructs a patient-specific 3D model of the coronary arteries, and applies computational fluid dynamics through its FFR analysis workflow to simulate blood flow and pressure across the coronary tree. The platform then calculates FFRCT values at every point to show whether a narrowing is functionally significant, and returns objective quantitative results to physicians in 5-10 minutes as a color-coded visualization rather than a purely manual read. Heartflow also uses Plaque analysis to quantify coronary plaque for earlier detection and prevention. The article says Heartflow continues to improve its models using a library of 110 million annotated CCTA images, indicating a large training data store feeding ongoing model refinement and clinical deployment.

data_flow: Coronary CTA image sets from CT scanners are uploaded into Heartflow, which reconstructs a 3D coronary model from thousands of images, runs FFR analysis to simulate flow and pressure, computes FFRCT values throughout the arteries, and serves quantitative visual results to physicians for triage and treatment decisions. Plaque analysis uses the same imaging foundation to quantify plaque burden for preventive care.
integration_points: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) image sets
business_outcome: Heartflow enables quicker and more precise CAD evaluation, achieves accuracy close to invasive functional assessment, supports triage for intermediate stenosis, helps physicians avoid unnecessary risky interventions, and has scaled to broad adoption across US hospitals and outpatient facilities.
metrics: approximately 1,400 of 2,700 US hospitals and outpatient facilities performing CCTA have already adopted the Heartflow platform
